searchText: You're right I think, but I don't know how we can handle this nicely in the spec, other than with just describing the behavior in words Maybe with `on_proposer_slashing`, like we set `equivocating_indices` with `on_attester_slashing`? Are proposer slashings produced by any node, since they're trivial to detect, or just by slashers? In other words, if my node receives two blocks from the same proposer, would I immediately produce a `proposer_slashing`, which could then be processed and do what we need in the fork-choice of the node? At least Nimbus doesn't detect proposer slashings Slashing detection is almost purely altruistic anyway (no, not block inclusion, but finding the slashings themselves) Having nodes produce proposer slashings upon detecting an equivocation in gossip seems like one way to get this information to the fork-choice, but if people prefer to just have a note that says you shouldn't apply proposer boost when an equivocation has been detected we can also do that. Or not sure what other alternatives there are, the bottom line is that trustless payments are vulnerable without detecting proposer equivocation and having proposer boost conditional on that Or alternatively have a fork-choice handler for equivocation detection on gossip, e.g. `on_proposer_equivocation`, to be called when detecting a second beacon block over gossip? Just to actually integrate the behavior in the fork-choice spec, while keeping `proposer_slashing` out of this
